title: INI-CET Recall Research + Adjustable-Difficulty Question-Generation Specification
purpose: Research-public recall collections and derive a careful MCQ-generation specification; not a validated official exam-paper dataset.

source_integrity.material_type: Memory-based and commercially reconstructed past-question recalls, with optional coaching-authored additions
source_integrity.verified_material: Inspected an AIIMS official July 2026 prospectus, sampled a directly accessible 49-page May 2026 recall PDF including images, read a 2022 medicine recall document in text form, reviewed indexed year/subject breakdowns and short 2024 PDF samples.
source_integrity.not_done: Did not acquire, audit, verify answer keys for, or calculate difficulty from every advertised online question; no statistical official difficulty or all-paper distribution is claimed.
source_integrity.cross_source_overlap_risk: First questions of 2026 DigiNerve PDF and the Oncourse 2026 page display matching stems, so the two sources cannot be added together as distinct questions.
source_integrity.historical_naming_warning: An archive advertising questions dating to 1994 can contain pre-INI-CET predecessor exam material; treat such items as historical medical entrance questions, not original INI-CET papers.
source_integrity.copyright_handling: This file contains analytical patterns and citations/URLs, not an unlicensed compilation of third-party copyrighted question texts.

recommended_question_generator.disclaimer: The following parameters are a proposed harder-than-recall training design, not measured frequencies or an officially validated INI-CET blueprint.
recommended_question_generator.source_imitation: Abstract the decision mechanism and distractor logic; do not closely paraphrase or reproduce substantial third-party questions.
recommended_question_generator.stem_length: Mix concise direct questions with moderate-length and select long clinical cases. Length alone must not determine difficulty.
recommended_question_generator.answer_options: Typically 4 well-designed alternatives; support officially permitted multiple-correct types. Avoid automatically translating AMC five-option patterns into INI-CET.
recommended_question_generator.distractors: Same clinical category, mechanism, management tier, imaging choice or formula; no obviously absurd options.
high_difficulty_methods: Anatomical relationships viewed from different orientations
Avoid clues from option length or grammar
recommended_question_generator.subject_weighting: Cover all core MBBS preclinical, paraclinical and clinical areas, but do not claim fixed official per-subject quotas. Allow user-configured weights; do not use biased internet recalls as the actual blueprint.
recommended_question_generator.randomization: Balance correct answer locations; vary question types across all four sections.
quality_assurance: Ensure one unequivocal best answer or precisely defined multiple-correct keys
Preserve original images or create correctly labelled new visuals before asking visually dependent questions
recommended_question_generator.answer_delivery: During mock show question first; release answer, rationales and cited teaching points after response or at review, as requested.
recommended_question_generator.difficulty_control: Use difficulty_engine.config.difficulty_level and difficulty_intensity, with challenge mode for harder-than-recall questions.

difficulty_engine.purpose: Control the intellectual difficulty of original practice MCQs independently of the actual exam format.

1.label: Foundation
1.example_task: Recognise a classic pattern or basic mechanism
1.stem_length_rule: Usually short; include only relevant facts

2.label: Standard exam
2.integration: One or two linked concepts; a clear discriminator
2.distractor_design: All clinically related, usually one close competitor
2.example_task: Best diagnosis or next step with one decisive finding

3.label: Hard
3.integration: Use paired mechanism and application, or diagnostic comparison
3.distractor_design: Two closely competing alternatives, differing in a decisive cue
3.example_task: Select investigation or management when options are superficially reasonable
3.stem_length_rule: Concise or moderate, occasional longer case

4.label: Very hard
4.integration: Link multiple domains, risk modifiers, timing, or interpretation
4.distractor_design: Three or four credible options; decisive constraints hidden in genuine clinical facts
4.example_task: Choose the safest option after interpreting clinical history, lab data and competing risks
4.stem_length_rule: Length only when information contributes to the decision

5.label: Extreme
5.integration: Nested reasoning with competing diagnoses/actions, management sequencing, or exceptions
5.distractor_design: Every alternative credible in a nearby scenario; one unequivocally correct for the actual facts
5.example_task: Resolve two-way ambiguity with a discriminating finding and timing or safety nuance
5.stem_length_rule: No irrelevant padding; complexity derives from reasoning not word count
5.target: unvalidated super-exam challenge, NOT a claim of actual exam difficulty

fine_tuning.difficulty_intensity_interpretation: Within a chosen level, 0 is the easiest permissible case and 100 the hardest permissible case; level governs upper bounds on reasoning steps and prevents unsupported edge-case minutiae.
difficulty_increase_order: make distractors closer while preserving a unique answer
increase the number of clinically relevant interacting constraints
require integrating at least two established facts
add genuine conditional decisions or time-sensitive prioritisation
add numerical or visual interpretation only when supported by real data/media
fine_tuning.floor_and_ceiling: Do not go beyond the core MBBS/AMC candidate competency merely to make an item obscure; if level 5 cannot be created accurately on a topic, report limitation or choose another high-value competency.

exam_faithful.description: Preserve official question type, subject domains, exam timing and exam-like difficulty distribution. User-selected global level is a target; do not claim it measures actual exam item parameters.

challenge.description: Preserve official question types and five/four choices while using the chosen level for most items. It is intentionally harder or easier than a representative exam.

adaptive_practice.description: Educational adaptation from observed answers, not official psychometrically calibrated CAT.

adaptive_practice_rules.increase_if: 3 consecutively correct answers with appropriate reasoning
adaptive_practice_rules.decrease_if: 2 consecutive incorrect answers or user reports guessing
adaptive_practice_rules.disclaimer: This is a teaching progression and is not equated to an official computerized adaptive test or a validated score.

clinical_integrity_checks: Resolve the question and identify the unique best answer before constructing distractors.
Independently re-check that the supplied stem contains adequate discriminating information.
For each incorrect option write the specific reason it fails in this scenario; revise if more than one is equally defensible.
Verify calculations, reference ranges, dosing, contraindications, clinical urgency and units.
For guideline-sensitive current recommendations, verify against authoritative locally applicable published guidance; flag any unverified detail.
Never treat a memory-based recall key or AI-generated explanation as an authoritative clinical reference.
Do not fabricate image, ECG, histology or radiology findings while claiming a real supplied image exists.
Randomise correct-option location across a batch and prevent answer-position clues.
Use original stems; do not copy or closely paraphrase protected third-party recall text.
If the item cannot be made both difficult and medically unambiguous, reduce difficulty or flag for human review.
generation_workflow: Load this file and accept user config overrides only for editable fields.
Select exam-specific official-safe question format and blueprint constraints.
Choose competency and clinically valid correct concept first.
Choose difficulty level and intensity; implement clinically defensible levers.
Create stem + exam-appropriate options + correct key privately.
Run two-pass quality control including a second solution attempt and distractor challenge.
Show question alone when answer is withheld; reveal explanation after user answers.
Repeat; for mocks follow specified exam timing and section lock behaviour.

question_output_schema.subject: string
question_output_schema.answerIndex: integer 0-based for single-best-answer; null if multiple-correct
question_output_schema.answerIndices: array of 0-based ints only for multiple-correct; otherwise null
reasoning_steps: brief teaching-level steps (not private model scratchpad)

level_4: multi-statement traps with independently assessable truth values
level_5: nonobvious exception supported by canonical principle
complex but precisely stated numerical or image interpretation

exam_specific_constraints.answer_format_note: Assertion/reason, match-the-following and multi-statement items may be presented within officially permitted answer-choice types. Do not claim they are separately defined exam modalities.

scoring.multiple_correct_partial_credit: Do not assume; apply only if confirmed by official rules.

exam_specific_constraints.image_based_rules: Include only actual readable embedded/retrieved user-authorised images or fully specified text/diagram descriptions if not presenting as image interpretation.
exam_specific_constraints.subject_weights: No verified official per-subject quotas; cover all core 19 MBBS subjects and integration; any practice distribution is a proposal, not an official weight.
exam_specific_constraints.navigation: Four independent timed sections; no return to earlier sections.
hardness_levers: two or more linked basic-science and clinical concepts
closely related embryology or anatomy structures
pathology pattern plus genetics or immunohistochemistry
epidemiology biostatistics with units and interpretations

generator_instructions: You are creating ORIGINAL INI-CET practice MCQs from this JSON profile. Use difficulty_engine.config and exam_specific_constraints. Treat difficulty_level (integer 1..5) as an editable control and difficulty_intensity (0..100) as a fine adjustment. Honor mode: exam_faithful for blueprint-style distribution; challenge for predominantly chosen difficulty; adaptive_practice for educational progression based on user answers. NEVER change exam option count, correct-answer rules, timing, or navigational sections just because difficulty increases. Each item must be medically defensible with one unique best answer unless the exam explicitly permits multiple-correct. Generate original questions inspired by concepts and structures, not literal copied PYQs. Verify answer against appropriate references where needed. If delivery=one_by_one, ask one question and hide the key until candidate answers; then present clear rationale and why attractive distractors are wrong. Do not label difficulty as officially calibrated. Do not pretend a text-described image is a real image.
